title: eludite.debug output
description: The debugger's state, as the Locals, Watch, Call Stack, Threads, Breakpoints and Exception Settings windows, the Output window's Debug source and the status bar show it: the whole model. eludite.debug.state, stop, toggle_breakpoint, select_frame, watch and exception_settings answer with it; the commands that run the debuggee answer with the smaller stop summary (debug-stop-summary.output.json).

mode.description: `design`: no session. `building`: F5 or Ctrl+F5 is building the startup project first (the setting build.beforeRun); the launch follows when the build succeeds, and the session goes back to `design` with `message` saying why when it fails or is canceled. `launching`: the adapter and the debuggee are starting (or the adapter is attaching, eludite.debug.attach). `running`: the debuggee runs (also while a step is in flight). `break`: stopped; the call stack, locals and watches are filled. `stopping`: the session is ending. `running_without_debugging`: started with Ctrl+F5.

generation.description: The session generation: it grows with every start. Events and answers of an older session are dropped.

stop.description: Grows every time the debuggee breaks. Quote it as `stop` in a command to have the command refused if the debuggee moved on since (another driver stepped).

project.description: The project file (a Cargo package's Cargo.toml); for an attached session, the process's name.

program.description: The program run: the built DLL of a .NET (Core) project, the built .exe of a .NET Framework project, the executable of a Cargo package's binary target or test executable (from cargo's compiler-artifact message). For an attached session, the process's program (its command line's first argument).

adapter.description: The debug adapter's executable and transport: `netcoredbg --interpreter=vscode (stdio)`, `eludite-dbg-mono under mono 6.8.0.105 (stdio)` (the version from `mono --version`), or `lldb-dap 18.1.3 (stdio)` (the version from `lldb-dap --version`, else from the `lldb --version` beside it; CodeLLDB reads `codelldb (stdio)`).

runtime.description: What runs the program: `coreclr` (.NET 5 and later, .NET Core: `dotnet`, debugged with netcoredbg), `mono` (a .NET Framework program run by the located Mono off Windows, debugged with eludite-dbg-mono), `netfx` (a .NET Framework program run directly on Windows, debugged with eludite-dbg-netfx once brief 0004 builds it), `native` (a Cargo package's executable, run directly and debugged with lldb-dap).

attached.description: The session attached to a running process (eludite.debug.attach): Stop detaches and the process keeps running; Restart is refused. Absent for a launch.

stopped.description: In break mode: why and where.

driver.description: Who resumed the debuggee before this stop: `user` or `agent:<name>`.

frames.description: The selected thread's call stack, top first (at most 200).

name.description: The method, as the Call Stack window shows it.

path.description: The source file, when the frame has one.

locals.description: The selected frame's locals, top level (at most 500); expand one with eludite.debug.evaluate and `expand`.

reference.description: Non-zero when the value has members; expand it by evaluating `evaluate_name` with `expand: true`.

evaluate_name.description: An expression that evaluates to this value.

kind.description: `line` (a breakpoint on a line), `tracepoint` (a line breakpoint with `log_message`: When Hit, print a message and continue) or `function` (a function breakpoint, by `function`; no path or line).

path.description: The source file (absent for a function breakpoint).

verified.description: The adapter bound it to code in the running session.

hits.description: Times it was reached in this session (a tracepoint's hits count its lines).

message.description: Why it is not bound, from the adapter.

remove_after.description: Deleted at its first visible stop ("Delete breakpoint when hit").

temporary.description: Set by eludite.debug.run_until or eludite.debug.trace for the length of that call and removed after it; never persisted. The Breakpoints window marks it.

breakpoints.description: The Breakpoints window's rows: line breakpoints and tracepoints by file and line, then function breakpoints by name.

break_on_rust_panic.description: The Exception Settings window's Rust panics row: a native (Cargo) session breaks when a Rust panic starts, through a function breakpoint on `rust_panic` (what rust-lldb users set). Default true; persisted with the other exception settings.

types.description: Exception types under Common Language Runtime Exceptions (eludite.debug.exception_settings `types`).

console.description: The program's output and the debugger's messages, as the Output window's Debug source shows them: how many lines the session wrote and the last ones (at most 20), and `next`, the cursor of the program's own lines (pass it as eludite.debug.output's `since` to read only what comes after). The standalone Debug Console window was retired by brief 0020.

next.description: The program output's next sequence number (eludite.debug.output, source `program`).

last_driver.description: Who issued the last command that changed the session: `user` or `agent:<name>`.

message.description: The last error or notice (for example why the adapter could not start).

capabilities.description: The debug adapter's capabilities, once a debugging session has started it (absent otherwise).

agent_driving.description: True when the last command that started, resumed or paused the debuggee came from an agent (`last_driver` starts with `agent:`); the status bar slot then ends with `, agent driving`.

agents_allowed.description: Whether agents may drive the session (Debug > Allow Agents to Drive, eludite.debug.allow_agents): while false, agents' commands that start, resume or change the session are refused and their reads keep working. Each session starts with the setting debugger.allowAgentsByDefault.

capabilities.description: What the session's debug adapter supports, so a caller does not try what it lacks. Booleans unless noted; `adapter` or `shell` where the shell provides what the adapter lacks.

pause.description: Debug > Break All (eludite.debug.pause); every adapter has it.

set_variable.description: Values can be changed (eludite.debug.set_variable: DAP setVariable, or setExpression when the adapter has only that).

function_breakpoints.description: Breakpoints on a function by name (DAP setFunctionBreakpoints); eludite.debug.toggle_breakpoint with `function` is refused where false.

log_points.description: Tracepoints: `adapter` (DAP logMessage) or `shell` (the debugger emulates them with a stop, the message's evaluation and a resume per hit).

hit_conditions.description: Hit counts on breakpoints: `adapter` or `shell` (the debugger counts hits itself).

exception_filter_options.description: Exception settings can name exception types (DAP exceptionFilterOptions); eludite.debug.exception_settings with `types` is refused where false.

set_next_statement.description: Set Next Statement (eludite.debug.set_next_statement: DAP gotoTargets and goto); refused where false.

data_breakpoints.description: Break when a value changes (DAP data breakpoints).

restart.description: The adapter restarts a session itself (DAP restart).

terminate.description: The debuggee can be asked to end gracefully (DAP terminate).

modules.description: Loaded modules can be listed (DAP modules).

delayed_stack_loading.description: The adapter pages call stacks itself (DAP supportsDelayedStackTraceLoading); otherwise the debugger reads the stack once and pages it.

variable_paging.description: The adapter pages variables by `start` and `count`; otherwise the debugger reads them all and pages.
